- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day windows.
- Underestimate when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment=0.00), but overcorrect when sentiment turns positive — adjust downward if sentiment rises sharply.
- Lagged mean reversion: if 18-day history shows strong upward trend, forecast should not overshoot beyond +3% above recent peak.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks > +5% above recent 18-day high, reduce by 1–3% in next 5–7 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate mid-term (days 15–25) when sentiment is flat — cap forecast at 1.5–2% below true outcome in those periods.
- No correction needed if sentiment remains 0.00 across 18-day history — model is neutral, no bias to adjust for.
